chapters.title: Judah’s rebellion and the call to return

parts.text: Isaiah’s vision concerns Judah and Jerusalem during four kings’ reigns. The LORD charges his people with rebellion despite his fatherly care; their wounded, devastated condition exposes their sin. Sacrifices, assemblies, and prayers are unacceptable while their hands are stained with blood. They must cease evil, learn justice, and defend the vulnerable. God offers cleansing and life to the willing, but warns the rebellious of destruction.

Jerusalem, once faithful, has become corrupt, with rulers who accept bribes and neglect orphans and widows. The LORD will purify his people as metal is refined, restore righteous judgment, and redeem Zion. Those who persist in idolatry and rebellion will instead perish.

chapters.title: The LORD’s mountain and the humbling of pride

parts.text: In the last days, the LORD’s house will be exalted and nations will come seeking his instruction. Law and the word of the LORD will go out from Zion and Jerusalem. His judgment will turn weapons into tools for cultivation, and nations will no longer learn war. Jacob is therefore called to walk in the LORD’s light.

The present people have filled their land with foreign practices, riches, weapons, and idols. A day of the LORD will bring down everything proud and exalted, leaving him alone honoured. People will hide among rocks and cast away their idols before his majesty. The chapter warns against placing ultimate confidence in frail human beings.

chapters.title: Failed leadership and Zion’s humiliation

parts.text: The LORD will remove Judah’s sustaining resources and capable leaders, leaving confusion, oppression, and people unwilling to accept rule over the ruins. Jerusalem’s words and deeds have opposed him, and the people’s open sin testifies against them. The righteous will receive good and the wicked the fruit of their actions. God calls leaders to account for consuming the vineyard and crushing the poor.

The proud daughters of Zion are then addressed. Their display of ornaments and luxury will be replaced by deprivation, shame, and mourning. Men will fall by the sword, and the city will sit desolate on the ground. Social arrogance and abuse are shown ending in the collapse of the society that sheltered them.

chapters.title: Cleansed Zion beneath God’s protection

parts.text: The preceding devastation leaves a severe imbalance in which seven women seek the name of one man, offering to supply their own food and clothing if their reproach can be removed. The scene continues the account of Jerusalem’s loss and humiliation.

A different prospect follows for Israel’s survivors. The branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and those remaining in Zion will be called holy after God washes away filth and bloodshed through judgment. The LORD will create cloud by day and flaming brightness by night over Zion’s dwellings and assemblies, providing shelter from heat, storm, and rain.

chapters.title: The vineyard that produced injustice

parts.text: A song describes a carefully planted and protected vineyard that yields wild grapes instead of the good fruit its owner expected. The owner will therefore remove its defences and allow it to become waste. The explanation is explicit: the vineyard is Israel, and Judah is the pleasant planting. God looked for judgment and righteousness but found oppression and a cry of distress.

Woes follow against greedy land accumulation, drunken indifference, defiant sin, moral inversion, self-conceit, and corrupt justice. Because the people rejected the LORD’s instruction, anger and judgment come upon them. A distant, disciplined nation is summoned, and its swift, relentless advance leaves the land in darkness and sorrow.

chapters.title: Isaiah sees the holy LORD and is commissioned

parts.text: In the year King Uzziah dies, Isaiah sees the Lord enthroned above the temple. Seraphims proclaim his holiness, the foundations tremble, and smoke fills the house. Isaiah fears destruction because he has unclean lips and belongs to a similarly unclean people. One of the seraphims touches his mouth with a live coal from the altar and declares his sin purged.

When the Lord asks whom to send, Isaiah volunteers. He is commissioned to address a people whose continued hearing will not bring understanding and whose hearts remain hardened. Asked how long, the LORD speaks of devastation, empty cities, and removal of inhabitants. Yet the image of a surviving tree stump preserves the prospect of a holy seed.

chapters.title: Ahaz receives a sign and a warning

parts.text: As Syria and Israel threaten Judah, Isaiah meets Ahaz and tells him not to fear their plan to replace David’s dynasty. Their scheme will not stand, but Ahaz must believe to be established. When he refuses the offer of a sign, the Lord gives one: a virgin will conceive and bear Immanuel. Before the child can distinguish good and evil, the land of the two feared kings will be forsaken.

The warning then turns toward Assyria, which the LORD will bring as an unprecedented affliction upon Judah. Images of flies, bees, a hired razor, and neglected farmland describe invasion and humiliation. Former vineyards will become briars, and survival will replace prosperity.

chapters.title: Assyria’s advance and the testimony of God

parts.text: Isaiah records the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, and his newborn son bears it as a sign that Damascus and Samaria will be plundered before he can call for his parents. The people’s rejection of Shiloah’s gentle waters is contrasted with Assyria’s overwhelming flood, reaching into Judah. Yet hostile alliances cannot finally overturn God’s presence with his people.

Isaiah is warned not to share the people’s fearful conspiracies, but to sanctify the LORD, who will be both sanctuary and a stone of stumbling. He preserves the testimony and waits for God, recognizing himself and his children as signs. Seeking the dead is rejected; instruction must be tested by God’s law and testimony, without which darkness follows.

chapters.title: A promised ruler and continuing judgment

parts.text: Light will shine upon people walking in darkness, bringing joy and release from oppression. A child is born and a son given whose government rests upon his shoulder. He is named Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, and The Prince of Peace. His righteous rule on David’s throne will increase without end through the LORD’s zeal.

The remainder addresses the pride and rebellion of Jacob and Israel. The people answer disaster with self-confident plans rather than returning to God. Misleading leaders, false prophets, wickedness, and mutual hostility bring successive judgments. The repeated declaration that God’s anger remains and his hand is still stretched out emphasizes their refusal to change.

chapters.title: Assyria is an instrument, not a sovereign power

parts.text: Unjust lawmakers are condemned for robbing the needy and denying rights to widows and orphans. Assyria is then described as the rod of God’s anger, sent against a sinful people. Its king, however, credits conquest to his own strength and intends indiscriminate destruction. God will punish that arrogance, as an axe cannot boast over the person wielding it.

A remnant of Israel will return and rely on the Holy One rather than its former oppressor. Zion is told not to fear Assyria, because God’s anger and the burden of foreign rule will end. The approaching army is traced through successive places toward Jerusalem, but the LORD cuts down the lofty forest of its power.

chapters.title: The branch from Jesse and the gathered remnant

parts.text: A shoot from Jesse’s roots receives the LORD’s spirit of wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and reverence. He judges the poor righteously rather than by appearances and strikes wickedness with the word of his mouth. Righteousness and faithfulness characterize him. Peace extends through the animal creation, and nothing harms on God’s holy mountain because knowledge of the LORD fills the earth.

The root of Jesse becomes an ensign sought by the Gentiles. God gathers Israel’s scattered remnant from many lands, ends rivalry between Ephraim and Judah, and brings victory over enemies. Barriers are removed and a highway prepared for the returning people, recalling Israel’s earlier deliverance from Egypt.

chapters.title: Songs drawn from the wells of salvation

parts.text: In that day, the people will praise the LORD because his anger has turned away and he has comforted them. God himself is their salvation, strength, and song, so trust replaces fear. Drawing water joyfully from the wells of salvation becomes an image of their renewed life. They are called to proclaim his deeds among the peoples, celebrate his excellent works throughout the earth, and rejoice because the Holy One of Israel is great in Zion’s midst.

chapters.title: The burden against Babylon

parts.text: A banner summons forces for the LORD’s judgment against Babylon. The coming day is described with terror, human anguish, darkened heavenly lights, and the shaking of earth and heaven. God will punish pride and wickedness, and violent invasion will leave people fleeing to their own lands while households suffer devastating losses.

The Medes are named as the force God stirs up, unmoved by silver or gold. Babylon’s splendor will become like Sodom and Gomorrah, overthrown and uninhabited. Wild creatures will occupy its ruined palaces instead of settled families and shepherds. The oracle insists that the appointed end will not be indefinitely delayed.

chapters.title: Babylon’s pride falls and Zion is preserved

parts.text: The LORD promises mercy and restoration to Jacob, followed by a taunt against Babylon’s fallen king. The former oppressor’s downfall gives the earth rest, while the dead mock his lost glory. The taunt addresses Lucifer, son of the morning, whose ambition to ascend above the stars and become like the most High ends in the pit. His ruined body, dynasty, and city expose the collapse of destructive pride.

The LORD also declares his purpose to break the Assyrian in his land and remove his yoke, a decision no one can reverse. A separate warning tells Palestina not to celebrate the breaking of one enemy’s rod, since another threat will arise. Zion’s security rests in the LORD who founded her.

chapters.title: Moab mourns its devastation

parts.text: Sudden destruction overtakes Moab’s cities, producing public mourning, shaved heads, sackcloth, and widespread cries. Even its armed men are shaken. The prophet expresses grief as fugitives flee toward Zoar and carry their possessions across the waters. Dry vegetation and failing streams deepen the misery. Lamentation reaches the borders of the land, yet further judgment remains: blood fills the waters of Dimon, and danger pursues those who escape. The oracle portrays both the thoroughness of Moab’s loss and sorrow over its suffering.

chapters.title: Moab’s pride and a deadline for its fall

parts.text: The chapter calls for tribute toward Zion and describes Moab’s daughters as displaced birds. Counsel is sought for sheltering outcasts and concealing fugitives from the destroyer. It also looks toward the end of oppression and a throne established in mercy in David’s tabernacle, occupied by one who seeks judgment and hastens righteousness.

Moab’s renowned pride is exposed as empty, and ruined vineyards and harvests become occasions for weeping. Songs and gladness disappear from the presses, while prayer at Moab’s sanctuary brings no rescue. The LORD specifies that within three years, measured like a hired worker’s term, Moab’s glory will be brought low and only a small, feeble remnant remain.

chapters.title: Damascus falls and Jacob is brought low

parts.text: Damascus will become a ruined heap, and its associated strongholds will lose their glory. Jacob too is pictured as wasted flesh and a harvested field, with only a few gleanings remaining. In that day people will look to their Maker, the Holy One of Israel, rather than altars and objects their own hands made.

Desolation follows because the people forgot the God of their salvation and the rock of their strength. Carefully cultivated plantings yield grief rather than security. The roaring of many nations is then compared to mighty waters, but God’s rebuke scatters them like chaff. Evening terror gives way to their disappearance before morning, the appointed outcome for plunderers.

chapters.title: A message concerning a distant people

parts.text: An oracle addresses a land beyond Ethiopia’s rivers, associated with wings, river vessels, and swift messengers. The message concerns a nation described as scattered, afflicted, and formidable, whose land rivers have spoiled. The inhabitants of the world are told to watch when a banner is raised and listen when the trumpet sounds.

The LORD quietly observes before intervening like one cutting shoots before harvest. The severed growth is left for birds and beasts. After this judgment, a gift from the people described will be brought to the LORD of hosts at Mount Zion. The chapter links divine intervention with an eventual act of worship.

chapters.title: Egypt’s judgment and eventual healing

parts.text: The LORD comes against Egypt, shaking its idols and courage. Internal conflict, failed counsel, and harsh rule accompany the drying of waters and the collapse of work dependent upon them. Fishermen, weavers, and advisers alike are confounded. Egypt’s supposed wisdom cannot explain the LORD’s purpose, and the country staggers without effective direction.

The vision then turns toward Egypt fearing the LORD, speaking Canaan’s language, and setting up an altar and witness to him. He hears its cry, sends a deliverer, smites and heals it, and receives its worship. Egypt and Assyria are joined by a highway and shared service, while Israel becomes a blessing with both nations under God’s favour.

chapters.title: Isaiah becomes a sign against reliance on Egypt

parts.text: When Assyria captures Ashdod, the LORD tells Isaiah to remove his sackcloth and shoes. His walking naked and barefoot serves for three years as a sign against Egypt and Ethiopia. Their young and old will be led away exposed as captives by Assyria, bringing humiliation to Egypt. Those who relied on these powers for rescue will be dismayed. The inhabitants of the coastland will recognize that the refuge they expected has failed and ask how they themselves can escape.

chapters.title: Watchmen announce judgment

parts.text: A distressing vision concerns the wilderness of the sea. Elam and Media are summoned, and the prophet trembles at the coming devastation. Amid preparations and urgent commands, a watchman observes approaching riders and announces that Babylon has fallen and its carved gods have been broken. The report is delivered as what Isaiah has heard from the LORD.

A brief message concerning Dumah asks the watchman about the night; his answer speaks of morning and continued night, with an invitation to inquire again. An oracle against Arabia calls for water and bread for fugitives escaping battle. Within a year, Kedar’s glory will fail and few of its mighty archers remain.

chapters.title: Jerusalem’s false security and a change of steward

parts.text: The valley of vision is pictured in turmoil while Isaiah mourns the devastation of his people. Jerusalem inspects weapons, fortifies walls, and secures water but fails to look to the One who shaped its circumstances. When the Lord calls for mourning and repentance, the people instead feast, accepting death as a reason for indulgence. Their refusal brings a solemn declaration of judgment.

Shebna is rebuked for preparing an impressive tomb and will be removed from office. Eliakim is appointed in his place, receiving authority pictured by the key of David’s house and a firmly fixed nail. Yet the closing warning speaks of a secured nail falling with its burden, qualifying confidence in human office.

chapters.title: Tyre’s commerce humbled and redirected

parts.text: The destruction of Tyre brings mourning to trading ships and distant commercial partners. The prosperous city that enriched nations will lose its strength, and its inhabitants must flee. The LORD has purposed this humiliation to bring the pride of earthly glory into contempt. Chaldean devastation supplies a warning as the ships lament their lost stronghold.

Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, then return to the activity pictured through a harlot’s song. The LORD will visit her, and her trading proceeds will no longer merely be stored for herself. Her merchandise will be set apart for those dwelling before the LORD, supplying sufficient food and lasting clothing.

chapters.title: The earth is judged and the LORD reigns

parts.text: The LORD empties and overturns the earth, with no social rank exempt from the devastation. Its inhabitants have defiled it by transgressing laws, changing ordinances, and breaking the everlasting covenant. Curse consumes the land; wine, music, and feasting fall silent, while the city is left shattered. Survivors resemble gleanings after a harvest.

Voices nevertheless rise in praise from distant places, even as the prophet laments continuing treachery. Terror, pit, and snare leave no easy escape; the earth reels under its transgression. The LORD punishes heavenly and earthly powers, gathers them for judgment, and reigns gloriously in Zion and Jerusalem before his elders.

chapters.title: A feast, swallowed death, and humbled pride

parts.text: The prophet praises the LORD for faithful purposes and wonderful works. A fortified city becomes a ruin, causing strong peoples to honour him and ruthless nations to fear him. God has been a refuge for the poor and needy, sheltering them from violent oppression like shade from scorching heat.

On his mountain the LORD prepares a rich feast for all peoples and removes the covering spread over the nations. He swallows up death in victory, wipes away tears, and removes his people’s reproach. Those who waited for him rejoice in salvation. Moab’s pride and strong defences, however, are brought down into the dust.

chapters.title: Trust, resurrection, and shelter during judgment

parts.text: A song in Judah celebrates a strong city whose defences are God’s salvation. The righteous nation enters, and the mind fixed upon the LORD receives peace because it trusts him. He brings the lofty city down for the poor to tread upon. His judgments teach righteousness, although the wicked may refuse to learn even when shown favour.

The people confess dependence on God after the failure of other lords and compare their distress to labour that has produced no deliverance. A promise declares that God’s dead will live and rise, calling those in dust to sing. His people are told to hide briefly until indignation passes, as the LORD comes to expose bloodshed and punish earth’s inhabitants.

chapters.title: The tended vineyard and the gathering trumpet

parts.text: The LORD will punish leviathan and slay the dragon in the sea. A renewed vineyard is then celebrated, guarded and watered continually by God. Rather than persisting as hostile briars, people are invited to take hold of his strength and make peace. Jacob will take root, Israel will blossom, and their fruit will fill the world.

Judgment purges Jacob’s iniquity and removes idolatrous altars, while the fortified city becomes deserted. The LORD nevertheless gathers his people individually from a broad region. A great trumpet sounds, and those perishing in Assyria or cast out in Egypt return to worship the LORD on the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

chapters.title: False refuges and the sure foundation in Zion

parts.text: Ephraim’s proud, drunken splendor is condemned as a fading flower beneath approaching judgment. The LORD will instead be glory and strength to his remnant. Priests and prophets also stagger through drink, rejecting instruction as though it were childish repetition. The rest God offered is refused, and the repeated word becomes an occasion for stumbling and captivity.

Jerusalem’s rulers boast of an agreement with death and shelter themselves in lies. The Lord answers by laying a tested, precious cornerstone in Zion and exposing their refuge to judgment. The warning urges them to stop mocking. Examples of a farmer’s varied methods then illustrate the purposeful wisdom of God’s instruction and work.

chapters.title: Ariel’s distress and the exposure of false worship

parts.text: Ariel, the city where David dwelt, faces siege and humiliation, yet its attacking multitude will vanish like a dream when the LORD intervenes. The people themselves suffer spiritual blindness: the vision becomes like a sealed book. Their lips honour God while their hearts remain far away, so their admired wisdom will be confounded.

Those who hide their plans from the LORD reverse the proper relationship between potter and clay. God promises a transformation in which the deaf hear, the blind see, and the meek rejoice, while violent and unjust people disappear. Jacob will no longer be ashamed, and those formerly mistaken will gain understanding and receive instruction.

chapters.title: Rejected counsel, promised mercy, and Assyria’s fall

parts.text: Judah’s leaders seek protection in Egypt without asking the LORD, carrying treasure toward a refuge that cannot profit them. The people reject true prophecy and request agreeable illusions. Their iniquity is compared to a wall ready to collapse. God offers salvation through returning and rest, and strength through quiet trust, but they choose swift horses and will flee before a stronger pursuit.

The LORD nevertheless waits to be gracious and promises answered cries, instruction, rejection of idols, and renewed abundance. His appearing brings healing to his people and terror to their enemies. With song and rejoicing, they witness judgment against the Assyrian, whose prepared place of burning is kindled by the LORD’s breath.

chapters.title: Egypt’s horses cannot replace the LORD

parts.text: Those who seek Egypt’s horses and chariots while refusing to seek the Holy One of Israel are warned of disaster. Egyptians are mortal and their horses mere flesh; when the LORD acts, helper and helped fall together. By contrast, the LORD will defend Jerusalem with the determination of a lion and the protection of hovering birds. Israel is called to return and discard its idols. The Assyrian will fall by a sword beyond human power, before the LORD whose fire is in Zion.

chapters.title: Righteous government and the Spirit’s renewal

parts.text: A king will reign in righteousness and princes administer just judgment, providing protection like shelter from wind and refreshing streams in dry country. Understanding and clear speech replace confusion. Fools and grasping deceivers will no longer receive false honour, while generous people are recognized by their generous purposes.

Complacent women are warned that fruitful fields and pleasant homes will fall into mourning and desolation. That condition lasts until the spirit is poured out from on high, transforming wilderness into fruitful ground. Judgment and righteousness then produce peace, quietness, and lasting assurance. God’s people dwell securely, with renewed opportunity for fruitful labour.

chapters.title: The destroyer judged and Zion made secure

parts.text: A treacherous destroyer is warned that plunder will return upon him. The people ask the LORD for grace, daily strength, and salvation in trouble. His exaltation fills Zion with judgment and righteousness. Broken treaties, deserted roads, and a mourning land reveal the crisis, but God announces that he will arise and consume the enemy’s proud plans.

Those in Zion tremble at the prospect of dwelling near consuming holiness. The righteous person is described through honest speech, rejection of oppressive gain, and refusal of evil. Such people will see the king in beauty and Jerusalem secure. The LORD himself is judge, lawgiver, and king; he saves, removes sickness, and forgives his people’s iniquity.

chapters.title: The LORD’s day of vengeance against Edom

parts.text: The nations and the whole earth are summoned to hear of the LORD’s indignation against their armies. Slain multitudes and the dissolving host of heaven portray the magnitude of judgment. His sword descends upon Idumea, and slaughter at Bozrah is compared to a great sacrifice. This is identified as a day of vengeance and a year of recompense for Zion’s controversy.

Edom’s land becomes burning pitch and lasting waste, inhabited by wild creatures instead of nobles and palaces. Thorns overrun its strongholds. The listeners are directed to the LORD’s book, because his mouth and spirit guarantee the appointed gathering and possession of these creatures throughout the desolated land.

chapters.title: The redeemed return on a holy highway

parts.text: The desert blossoms and rejoices, displaying the LORD’s glory. Weak hands and trembling knees are strengthened by the announcement that God comes with recompense to save his people. Blind eyes open, deaf ears hear, the lame leap, and the speechless sing. Waters transform the wilderness into a place of life. A highway called the way of holiness is prepared for the redeemed, safe from destructive beasts. The LORD’s ransomed return to Zion with songs and everlasting joy, while sorrow and sighing disappear.

chapters.title: Assyria challenges Jerusalem’s trust

parts.text: During Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib captures Judah’s fortified cities and sends Rabshakeh to Jerusalem with a large force. He challenges the city’s confidence, dismisses Egypt as a broken reed, and misrepresents Hezekiah’s removal of other altars as an offence against the LORD. He even claims that the LORD authorized Assyria’s attack.

Judah’s officials ask him to speak privately in the Syrian language, but he addresses the people loudly in their own tongue. He urges surrender, promises provision followed by relocation, and says no nation’s god has rescued it from Assyria. By Hezekiah’s command the people give no answer, and the officials report the threats with torn clothes.

chapters.title: The LORD answers Hezekiah and defeats Assyria

parts.text: Hezekiah mourns, enters the LORD’s house, and sends officials to Isaiah. The prophet assures him that the blasphemous threat will fail. When a renewed message claims Jerusalem’s God cannot save it, Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD and prays. He acknowledges Assyria’s real conquests but distinguishes lifeless idols from the living Creator, asking rescue so all kingdoms may know him.

Isaiah delivers the LORD’s answer: Assyria’s arrogance has forgotten that its power was permitted by God. The king will be turned back, and Jerusalem defended for God’s own sake and David’s. An angel strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib returns home and is later killed by his sons while worshiping his god.

chapters.title: Hezekiah’s recovery and thanksgiving

parts.text: When Hezekiah becomes mortally ill, Isaiah tells him to set his house in order because he will die. Hezekiah weeps and prays, and the LORD sends a new word granting fifteen additional years and promising protection from Assyria. As a confirming sign, the shadow on Ahaz’s sundial moves backward ten degrees.

Hezekiah’s written thanksgiving recalls his fear of losing the remainder of life and no longer praising God among the living. He compares the threatened end to a removed tent and cut weaving, then celebrates deliverance and forgiven sins. He promises praise in the LORD’s house. The account also records Isaiah’s instruction to apply a lump of figs to the boil.

chapters.title: Babylon’s visitors and a warning of exile

parts.text: After hearing of Hezekiah’s illness and recovery, Babylon’s king sends letters and a gift. Hezekiah welcomes the envoys and shows them all his treasures, weapons, and resources. Isaiah questions him, then announces that everything displayed will one day be carried to Babylon, with some of his descendants serving as eunuchs in its royal palace. Hezekiah acknowledges the LORD’s word as good and speaks of peace and truth during his own days, though the warning reaches beyond his lifetime.

chapters.title: Comfort from the incomparable Creator

parts.text: God commands comfort for his people and announces that Jerusalem’s appointed hardship is fulfilled. A voice calls for preparation of the LORD’s way, with valleys raised and heights lowered so his glory is revealed. Human glory fades like grass, but God’s word endures. Zion is to proclaim the coming Lord, who rules mightily yet gathers and gently leads his flock.

The chapter contrasts the Creator’s immeasurable wisdom and power with nations, rulers, and handmade idols. He names and sustains the stars and cannot be compared with anything people fashion. Israel must not assume its way is hidden from him. The everlasting God does not grow weary and renews the strength of those who wait upon him.

chapters.title: Israel upheld while idols fail the test

parts.text: The nations are summoned to consider the LORD’s rule over history and the conqueror he raises. Israel, his chosen servant and the offspring of Abraham his friend, is told not to fear. God holds and strengthens his people, overthrows their adversaries, and transforms their weakness into effective power. He supplies water and trees in barren places so observers recognize his hand.

Idols are then challenged to demonstrate their claim by explaining former events or declaring what will come. They cannot produce meaningful counsel or accomplish good or evil. The LORD, by contrast, announces and carries out his purpose. The chapter ends by exposing the idols and their works as emptiness and confusion.

chapters.title: The servant’s justice and Israel’s blindness

parts.text: The LORD presents his Spirit-endowed servant, who brings judgment to the Gentiles without crushing the bruised or extinguishing the faintly burning. He is appointed as a covenant to the people and light to the Gentiles, opening blind eyes and freeing prisoners. A new song celebrates God’s action, while he goes forth against enemies and leads the blind along unfamiliar paths.

Attention then turns to the blindness and deafness of the LORD’s own servant people. Though they have seen much, they fail to observe; plunder and imprisonment expose their condition. The LORD gave Jacob to the robbers because they refused his ways and law. Even the burning force of judgment has not yet been taken to heart.

chapters.title: The Redeemer gathers his witnesses

parts.text: The LORD tells Jacob not to fear, for he created, redeemed, and called his people by name. He promises presence through waters and fire and gathers sons and daughters from every direction. Israel is called to be his witness before the nations: no other god precedes or follows him, there is no saviour apart from the LORD, and no one can prevent his work.

He announces deliverance from Babylon and a new way through wilderness, recalling yet surpassing the former passage through the sea. Still, Israel has wearied him with sins rather than honoured him faithfully. He blots out transgressions for his own sake, while reminding them that ancestral and priestly rebellion has brought curse and reproach.

chapters.title: The Maker exposes idols and names Cyrus

parts.text: The LORD promises water for the thirsty and his spirit and blessing upon Jacob’s offspring. As Israel’s redeemer, first and last, he challenges any rival to declare his works. A long description exposes idol-making: a craftsman uses part of a tree for fuel and food, then worships the remainder as a god. Delusion prevents him from recognizing the contradiction.

Israel is told to remember its Maker and return because its sins have been blotted out. Creation is summoned to rejoice in redemption. The LORD frustrates false signs, confirms his servants’ word, and promises Jerusalem’s rebuilding. He names Cyrus as his shepherd, the one who will perform his pleasure concerning the city and temple foundations.

chapters.title: Cyrus commissioned and all the earth invited to salvation

parts.text: The LORD addresses Cyrus as his anointed instrument, promising to open doors, subdue kings, and reveal hidden treasures for Jacob’s sake. Cyrus is named although he has not known God, so the world may recognize that there is no other LORD. The LORD declares that he forms the light, creates darkness, makes peace, and creates evil. He rebukes creatures who contend with their Maker. Cyrus will rebuild the city and release captives without payment.

The nations’ recognition is contrasted with the shame of idol makers, while Israel receives everlasting salvation. God did not create the earth in vain or speak deceptively. He calls the ends of the earth to look to him and be saved; every knee will bow and every tongue acknowledge him.

chapters.title: The God who carries his people

parts.text: Bel and Nebo stoop as their idols become heavy loads for animals and go into captivity. Unlike these gods that must be carried, the LORD has carried Israel from birth and promises to bear and deliver his people into old age. He challenges comparison with idols manufactured from precious metal, transported by worshippers, and unable to answer or save.

The people are told to remember that the LORD alone is God. He declares the end from the beginning and accomplishes his counsel, summoning his chosen instrument from afar. To those stubbornly distant from righteousness, he announces that his righteousness is near and his salvation will not delay, bringing glory to Israel in Zion.

chapters.title: Babylon’s confidence collapses

parts.text: Babylon is ordered to leave her throne and sit in the dust, exchanging luxury for humiliating labour and exposure. The LORD will take vengeance as Israel’s redeemer. Though he delivered his people into Babylon’s hand, she showed no mercy, especially to the aged, and assumed her dominion would last forever.

Her proud claims of unmatched security cannot prevent sudden loss, widowhood, and desolation. Trust in wickedness, cleverness, and hidden action has deceived her. The chapter challenges her enchantments, astrologers, and monthly prognosticators to save her, but they are like stubble before fire. Those associated with her scatter, leaving no one able to rescue her.

chapters.title: Stubborn Israel is called to hear and leave Babylon

parts.text: The LORD addresses people who invoke his name without truth or righteousness. He declared events beforehand so their stubbornness could not credit idols after fulfilment. He now announces new things they could not claim to have known. Despite their treachery, he restrains anger and refines them in affliction for his own name’s sake, refusing to surrender his glory.

As Creator and ruler of history, he calls them to listen to the One who teaches and leads for their good. Obedience would have brought peace like a river and abundant descendants. They are now told to depart Babylon and proclaim redemption, remembering wilderness provision. The chapter closes by denying peace to the wicked.

chapters.title: A servant for Israel and the nations

parts.text: The servant speaks of being called from the womb and prepared like a sharp sword and hidden arrow. Though his labour seems fruitless, his judgment rests with the LORD. His mission extends beyond restoring Jacob: he becomes a light to the Gentiles and salvation to earth’s ends. The despised servant receives honour, and God’s covenant work releases prisoners and brings the gathered people home.

Zion fears she has been forgotten, but God compares his care to a mother’s love and says her walls are continually before him. Her returning children will overflow her former desolation. Kings and nations assist their return, and even captives of the mighty will be rescued, revealing the LORD as Saviour and Redeemer.

chapters.title: The obedient servant trusts amid suffering

parts.text: The LORD challenges Israel to explain its alienation. The people were not sold because God lacked resources; their own sins caused separation. His power to redeem remains undiminished, as shown by his command over sea, rivers, and heavens. Their failure was not caused by any weakness in his hand.

The speaker then describes receiving a taught tongue and an opened ear from the Lord GOD. He does not rebel, even when beaten, shamed, and spat upon. Confidence in divine help makes him steadfast before accusers. Those who fear the LORD are urged to trust through darkness, while those depending on their own kindled light are warned of sorrow.

chapters.title: Everlasting salvation and the removed cup of wrath

parts.text: Those pursuing righteousness are called to remember Abraham and Sarah, from whom God raised a multitude. Zion’s waste places will become like Eden, filled with thanksgiving. God’s instruction, judgment, and enduring salvation reach the peoples, outlasting heaven, earth, and human reproach. A plea for the LORD’s arm to awake recalls the defeat of Rahab and the passage through the sea, anticipating the ransomed returning with joy.

God comforts his people and challenges their fear of mortal oppressors. Jerusalem is told to awake from the staggering caused by his wrath, which left her without a guide. The Lord takes that cup from her hand and gives it to those who afflicted and humiliated her.

chapters.title: Zion’s release and the servant’s exaltation

parts.text: Zion is called to awake, put on beauty, and rise from captivity. The LORD will redeem his people without money, making his name known after foreign oppression. A messenger announces peace, salvation, and God’s reign; watchmen and ruins join in joy. All earth’s ends see his salvation. Those leaving captivity must depart cleanly, with the LORD going before and guarding behind them.

The focus turns to the LORD’s servant, who will act wisely and be highly exalted. His appearance has been marred beyond ordinary human recognition, yet he will sprinkle many nations. Kings become silent before an unprecedented revelation, preparing for the following account of his suffering.

chapters.title: The servant bears the sins of many

parts.text: The report describes a servant who grows without outward splendor and is rejected, sorrowful, and despised. Observers initially regard his suffering as God’s punishment upon him, but come to recognize that he bears their griefs and is wounded for their transgressions. His chastisement brings peace and healing. All have wandered like sheep, and the LORD lays their iniquity upon him.

Oppressed yet silent like a lamb led to slaughter, he is cut off from the land of the living and assigned a grave despite innocence. His soul becomes an offering for sin, and the LORD’s purpose prospers through him. The righteous servant justifies many, bears their sins, and intercedes for transgressors, receiving an honoured portion.

chapters.title: The forsaken wife restored in lasting mercy

parts.text: The barren woman is called to rejoice and enlarge her tent because her children will increase. Former shame will be forgotten: her Maker is her husband and the Holy One of Israel her redeemer. The brief experience of forsaking and wrath gives way to great mercy and everlasting kindness. God’s covenant of peace is compared with his oath concerning Noah’s waters.

The afflicted city will be rebuilt with precious materials, and her children taught by the LORD and established in peace. Righteousness replaces oppression and fear. God remains sovereign over both the craftsman who makes weapons and the destroyer. No weapon or accusing tongue will finally prevail against his servants, whose righteousness comes from him.

chapters.title: Come freely and return to the LORD

parts.text: Everyone who thirsts is invited to receive water, wine, and milk without payment. The people are asked why they spend effort on what cannot satisfy, and urged to listen so their souls may live. God promises an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, and a witness and leader whose call reaches nations formerly unknown.

The LORD should be sought while he may be found. The wicked must forsake their ways and thoughts and return to abundant pardon. God’s thoughts and ways exceed human ones, and his word accomplishes its purpose as rain makes the earth fruitful. Joyful departure, peace, and transformed vegetation become an enduring sign of his name.

chapters.title: A house of prayer and a rebuke to blind watchmen

parts.text: The LORD calls for justice because his salvation is near. Those who keep the sabbath and hold to his covenant are blessed. Foreigners and eunuchs must not regard themselves as excluded: faithful eunuchs receive an enduring name, and joined strangers are welcomed to the holy mountain. God’s house is to be a house of prayer for all peoples, with further gathering beyond Israel’s outcasts.

The tone changes to a summons of beasts and an indictment of Israel’s watchmen. Blind, silent, and sleep-loving, they cannot guard the flock. Greedy shepherds pursue their own gain and indulge in drink, confidently assuming tomorrow will repeat and enlarge their pleasures.

chapters.title: Idolatry exposed and the contrite revived

parts.text: The righteous may die without others realizing that they are being removed from coming evil and entering peace. By contrast, the people addressed as unfaithful practice idolatry, sacrifice children, and seek lovers and foreign help. They have forgotten the LORD and mistaken his silence for permission. Their gathered idols cannot rescue them, but trust in him brings inheritance.

The high and holy One also dwells with the humble and contrite, reviving their hearts. He will not contend forever, lest the spirits he made fail. Having chastened greed and stubbornness, he promises healing, guidance, and peace to those near and far. The wicked remain like a troubled sea that cannot rest, without peace.

chapters.title: The fast God chooses

parts.text: The prophet must expose sins among people who outwardly seek God and complain that their fasting goes unnoticed. Their fasts coexist with exploitation, quarrels, and violence. The LORD rejects self-affliction as a substitute for righteousness. His chosen fast loosens oppression, frees the burdened, shares bread with the hungry, shelters the homeless, and clothes the naked without neglecting one’s own kin.

Such conduct is joined with promises of light, healing, answered prayer, guidance, and restored ruins. The people must remove accusation and wicked speech and satisfy the afflicted. Honouring the sabbath rather than using it for personal business and pleasure will lead to delight in the LORD and enjoyment of Jacob’s inheritance.

chapters.title: Sin separates, but the LORD brings redemption

parts.text: The LORD can hear and save, but the people’s iniquities have separated them from him. Bloodshed, lies, corrupt judgment, violent schemes, and crooked paths show why peace is absent. The people confess that justice is far away; they grope like the blind and acknowledge their multiplied transgressions. Truth fails in public, and those who leave evil become prey.

Seeing no adequate intercessor, the LORD acts by his own arm, clothed in righteousness, salvation, vengeance, and zeal. He repays adversaries and makes his name feared from east to west. The Redeemer comes to Zion and to those in Jacob who turn from transgression. His covenant preserves his spirit and words among their descendants.

chapters.title: Zion rises in the LORD’s glory

parts.text: Zion is called to rise and shine as the LORD’s glory appears over her amid the world’s darkness. Nations and kings come to her light, bringing her scattered sons and daughters and the wealth of distant lands. Foreigners rebuild her walls, kings serve, and her gates remain open to receive their gifts. Former oppressors bow before the city of the Holy One of Israel.

Instead of abandonment, she receives enduring excellence, peace, and righteousness. Violence and devastation disappear, and her walls and gates are named Salvation and Praise. The LORD becomes her everlasting light, ending mourning and eclipsing dependence on sun and moon. Her righteous people inherit the land, and their increase occurs in his appointed time.

chapters.title: Good tidings and the restoration of Zion

parts.text: The Spirit of the Lord GOD rests upon a speaker whom the LORD has anointed to proclaim good news to the meek, bind broken hearts, and announce liberty to captives. His message includes the LORD’s acceptable year, the day of God’s vengeance, and comfort for mourners. Zion’s ashes and heaviness are exchanged for beauty, joy, and praise, making her people a righteous planting that glorifies God.

They rebuild old ruins and receive an honoured place among nations as the LORD’s priests and ministers. God promises an everlasting covenant and publicly recognizable blessing. Rejoicing follows in garments of salvation and righteousness, which God causes to spring up before all nations like growth in a garden.

chapters.title: Jerusalem will no longer be forsaken

parts.text: For Zion’s sake, the speaker will not be silent until her righteousness and salvation shine openly. Nations and kings will see her glory, and she will receive a new name from the LORD. No longer called Forsaken or Desolate, she is pictured as a cherished bride and a royal crown in God’s hand.

Watchmen are appointed to continue calling upon the LORD until Jerusalem becomes a praise in the earth. He swears that enemies will no longer consume her harvests; those who gather them will enjoy them in his holy courts. A highway is prepared and a proclamation announces salvation. The people are called holy and redeemed, and the city sought out rather than abandoned.

chapters.title: The divine warrior and a plea for remembered mercy

parts.text: A glorious figure approaches from Edom with garments stained as by a winepress. He identifies himself as speaking righteousness and mighty to save. He has trodden the peoples in anger without human assistance because the day of vengeance and year of redemption had come. His own arm accomplished salvation while judgment answered opposition.

The speaker recalls the LORD’s lovingkindness, care, and redemption of Israel, but acknowledges the people’s rebellion against his holy Spirit. Memories of Moses, the divided waters, and wilderness guidance become a prayer for renewed compassion. Calling God their Father and redeemer, the people ask him to return for his servants’ sake and remember the sanctuary trampled by their enemies.

chapters.title: A prayer for God to come down

parts.text: The people ask God to tear open the heavens and come down so mountains tremble and nations recognize his name. They recall wonders beyond expectation and his readiness to meet those who rejoice in righteousness. Yet they confess uncleanness, fading strength, and iniquities that carry them away like wind. Their failure to call upon him accompanies the hiding of his face.

They nevertheless appeal to him as Father and potter, acknowledging that all are the work of his hand. They ask that anger not continue forever and that sin not be continually remembered. Zion, Jerusalem, and the holy house lie desolate or burned, prompting a final plea that God not remain silent amid such affliction.

chapters.title: Rebellious worshippers and the promise of a new creation

parts.text: The LORD contrasts his readiness to be found with a people who continually provoke him through forbidden worship, unclean practices, and self-righteous exclusion. Judgment will repay their sins, yet he will preserve a seed rather than destroy all. His servants will eat, drink, and rejoice, while those who forsake him face hunger, shame, and death. Truth and a new name accompany his blessing.

God announces new heavens and a new earth and creates Jerusalem as a joy. Weeping gives way to long life, secure homes, fruitful labour, and answered prayer. The child shall die an hundred years old, but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed. Wolf and lamb feed together, and nothing harms or destroys in God’s holy mountain.

chapters.title: Humble worship, Zion’s comfort, and final judgment

parts.text: The LORD, whose throne is heaven and footstool earth, looks with favour upon the humble person who trembles at his word. Chosen rebellion makes outward sacrifices abhorrent. Those who mock the faithful will be ashamed, while Zion’s sudden birth brings joy. God promises comfort like a mother’s care and peace like a river, revealing his hand to his servants.

The LORD comes in fire to judge, distinguishing obedience from corrupt worship. He gathers nations to see his glory and sends survivors to proclaim it among distant peoples, bringing brethren to Jerusalem. As the new heavens and earth endure, so will his people’s name and offspring. All flesh comes to worship, while the unquenched judgment upon rebels remains a dreadful warning.
